meta.title: Water Day in the Square
meta.textType: functional: a news report, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by Lily and May. Today, Friday, April sixteenth, the town's water play afternoon was held in the town square. It began at two o'clock and ended at five o'clock. About eight hundred people came because the day was very hot. The square was crowded with local families, teenagers, and small children. They carried buckets, water pistols, and hoses. Water was thrown and sprayed all over the square. A banner across the square said, "Water Day: two o'clock to five o'clock." Tom and Ben, both thirteen, stood at a long table. They filled buckets with water. They also gave cups of water to the smaller children.

A pop band played on a small stage near the fountain. The music was noisy, and the children danced in the spray. A well-known pop singer, a celebrity in our town, came with a yellow water pistol. She sang one special song for the children. Then she sprayed the front row. She got wet like everyone else. Everybody laughed, and a little boy sprayed her back.

A police officer closed the road next to the square at two o'clock. He stood beside a sign at the side of the road. "Please do not throw water at motorbikes, and do not use ice water," he said. Water on a motorbike is dangerous, because the driver cannot see the road. Ice water may give a person a shock. So it is not allowed at the event. A grandmother in a flowered blouse stood near him with a small bowl of water. "Why do I come every year?" she asked us. "Everyone looks after themselves and each other," she said.

We asked Tom and Ben about the water table. "The table was busy, because small children cannot fill a bucket alone," said Tom. "So we filled the buckets for them." "I want to come again next year," Ben told us. Another group of teenagers carried the empty buckets back to the table. Their help kept the table full of water, so the line was short. The noisy afternoon was a happy festival for the whole town.

At five o'clock, the music stopped. The road was opened again, and the police officer smiled. The teenagers cleaned the square, so it was clean again by six o'clock. May asked the questions, and Lily wrote the post. It was a special day for the two of us, too. What was your favorite part of the day? Tell us in the comments.
